code:
# Lambda calculus: the theory of computation from 1936.
# THREE rules: variables, functions, application.
# ZERO primitives: no numbers, no booleans, no loops. Just functions.

# Yet here are Church booleans, built from nothing:
TRUE  = lambda x: lambda y: x   # select first
FALSE = lambda x: lambda y: y   # select second
IF    = lambda b: lambda t: lambda f: b(t)(f)

print("Church booleans:")
print(f"  TRUE  selects first:  {IF(TRUE)('yes')('no')}")
print(f"  FALSE selects second: {IF(FALSE)('yes')('no')}")

# Church numerals, natural numbers as functions:
ZERO  = lambda f: lambda x: x        # apply f 0 times
ONE   = lambda f: lambda x: f(x)     # apply f 1 time
TWO   = lambda f: lambda x: f(f(x))  # apply f 2 times
SUCC  = lambda n: lambda f: lambda x: f(n(f)(x))  # add one more application
ADD   = lambda m: lambda n: lambda f: lambda x: m(f)(n(f)(x))

to_int = lambda n: n(lambda x: x+1)(0)  # decode: apply successor to 0, n times

THREE = SUCC(TWO)
FIVE  = ADD(TWO)(THREE)

print(f"\nChurch numerals:")
print(f"  to_int(ZERO)  = {to_int(ZERO)}")
print(f"  to_int(THREE) = {to_int(THREE)}")
print(f"  to_int(FIVE)  = {to_int(FIVE)}")
print(f"  2 + 3 = {to_int(ADD(TWO)(THREE))}")

# Y combinator, recursion from scratch:
Y = lambda f: (lambda x: f(lambda v: x(x)(v)))(lambda x: f(lambda v: x(x)(v)))
factorial_logic = lambda self: lambda n: 1 if n <= 0 else n * self(n-1)
factorial = Y(factorial_logic)
print(f"\nY combinator factorial(5) = {factorial(5)}")

print("\n>>> This is the deep foundation the whole course builds toward.")
description: A 38-line program builds Church booleans, Church numerals with arithmetic, and the Y combinator for recursion entirely from lambda expressions with no primitives.

steps.description: The header comments state the three rules of lambda calculus (variables, functions, application) and zero primitives. Lines 6-8 define Church booleans: TRUE selects first argument, FALSE selects second, IF applies a boolean to two branches.
The boolean demo prints: TRUE selects first 'yes', FALSE selects second 'no'.

Church numerals encode natural numbers as repeated function application: ZERO applies f zero times, ONE once, TWO twice. SUCC adds one more application; ADD composes two numerals. to_int decodes by applying successor to 0.
SUCC wraps n in an extra f application. ADD threads f through m then n applications, giving m+n total applications.
Numeral demo prints: to_int(ZERO)=0, to_int(THREE)=3, to_int(FIVE)=5, and 2+3=5.
The Y combinator enables recursion without self-reference. factorial_logic takes a self parameter; Y applies it to itself via the classic fixed-point construction. factorial(5) computes 120.
The final output shows Y combinator factorial(5) = 120, demonstrating full recursion from pure lambda calculus.

title: Lambda Calculus Foundations: Booleans, Numerals, and Recursion
